items.title: Run when my AI limit resets, and continue on the backup engine
items.body:
## What the person gets

- **A new automation "when": the AI limit resets.** "When your Claude limit resets, Scout finishes the report." Once (default) or every reset. From chat ("run this when my limit resets" → `create_trigger when=limit_reset`), from the editor's When ("When my AI limit resets" + engine picker + once / every time), and from the calendar.
- **The stopped turn's button.** A turn stopped by a usage limit with a known reset shows **"Continue at 3:40 PM when your limit resets"**. One click creates a one-time limit-reset automation in that conversation (the usual card with Pause, Edit, Undo). It runs in that same conversation and is told the previous turn hit the limit.
- **The bot does it itself.** TRIGGER_PROMPT and the tool description cover it; a turn on an engine at ≥ 90 % has that on its clock line ("Claude's usage limit is 92% used; it resets …"), so the bot can set up its continuation and say so (no approval card, like every trigger).
- **Near-limit warning.** "Claude: 92% used · resets 3:40 PM" on the Automations page with **Move to after reset** for schedules due before the reset whose bot uses that engine (only their next run moves), plus a compact notice in that bot's chat header.
- **Calendar.** Each engine's next known reset is a labelled marker ("Claude resets 3:40 PM"). Dropping a bot from the sidebar on it opens the quick composer for a limit-reset automation; dropping an automation on it switches it to run at that reset.
- **Backup engine.** With Automatic recovery on and a backup configured (bot fallback list or workspace backup), a usage-limit refusal continues on the backup with one line: "Claude hit its limit (resets 3:40 PM), so Codex took over." After the reset, the next turn in that conversation goes back, with one line. No allowed backup → the Continue button. **Never** moves to another sign-in of the same subscription engine (that circumvents provider usage limits); another engine or a pay-per-use key is fine.

## How the reset time is derived

Schedule: `{ type: "limit_reset", engine, repeat: "once" | "every_reset", at }`. `at` is derived on the server (reset + 60 s), never taken from input; `null` while unknown.

`server/limit-resets.ts` keeps one limit per engine instance:
- **Plan usage** (`plan-usage.ts`): Claude `five_hour` / `seven_day` (`utilization`, `resets_at`); Codex `primary_window` / `secondary_window` (`used_percent`, `reset_at`, assigned by window length).
- **Refusals:** Claude's `rate_limit_info.resetsAt` (`runtime.error.limitResetsAt`); Codex now also sets `limitResetsAt` from its words "try again at 5:23 PM" / "…at Oct 17th, 2026 5:23 PM" (host local time).
- Rule: windows at ≥ 100 % decide and the latest of their resets counts; otherwise the fullest window. A live refusal wins unless usage shows a later window still full; it is kept 10 min past its time. Unknown → "runs when the limit resets (time not known yet)" and usage is polled every 5 min while an automation waits. Every usage refresh or refusal retimes the waiting automations. `every_reset` never runs twice for one reset.
- Usage is read at most every 5 minutes for the warnings. Sealed test fixtures no longer read this machine's keychain for plan usage.

## Failover

- Claude's startup hold, which already proves a signed-out refusal, also proves a usage-limit refusal (synthetic `usage_limit_reached` + error result with no new cost, process stopped) → `TurnUsageLimitRefusedError` → `startTurn`'s existing backup path.
- An engine the clock knows is refusing raises the same error before dispatch, so Codex/Grok turns and automation runs also go to the backup without spending a refused turn. A Codex automation run refused with a known reset is restarted at once for the backup instead of waiting for the reset.
- `limit-failovers.json` remembers `{thread → from, to, resetsAt}` for the switch back.

## Moved out (pinned files shrink)

`routine-schedules.ts` (from routines.ts), `routine-request-schemas.ts` (from routine-requests.ts), `routine-run-card.ts` (from index.ts), `projectCalls` → `lib/routine-calendar.ts`, ChatView's lucide import on one line. Pins lowered: index.ts 17285→17259, routines.ts 1804→1651, routine-requests.ts 1677→1484, ChatView.tsx 1492→1482, RoutineCalendarPage.tsx 1763→1750. store.tsx, App.tsx, electron/main.mjs unchanged. Catalog goldens re-pinned (create_trigger `when` + `engine` + `repeat`; budgets within 2 %).

## Tests

- `server/limit-resets.test.ts`: derivation from Claude and Codex fixtures, blocked vs fullest, refusal precedence, expiry, unknown time, Codex words, near-limit line.
- `server/routines-limit-reset.test.ts`: derived time, recompute when the reset moves, once vs every reset, unknown time, late wake still runs, restart, Move to after reset, backup restart of a refused run.
- `server/limit-reset-requests.test.ts`: create_trigger `when=limit_reset`, the card and Undo, default engine, duplicates, resume, and the routes (Continue creates the automation in the same thread, idempotent; after-reset; limits list).
- `server/drivers/claude-auth-recovery.test.ts`: the usage-limit refusal hold.
- `server/limit-failover.test.ts`: same-engine sign-ins refused, API key allowed, switch back after reset, unknown reset waits an hour.
- `server/limit-reset.e2e.test.ts` (real server, fake Claude/Codex, a test clock hook that shortens the post-reset minute): button → automation → reset → run continues the same conversation; failover to Codex with the line, pre-dispatch skip, switch back after reset; a same-engine backup is never used and the button is offered.
- `src/components/limit-resets.test.ts`: warning + Move to after reset, chat notice, Continue button, calendar marker and drops onto it, sentences.
- Mutation-checked: 36 unit-level and 7 end-to-end mutations, each caught.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added visibility into AI engine usage limits, including near-limit warnings and expected reset times.
  * Added automations that run once or repeatedly after an engine’s usage limit resets. Create and manage them from the calendar, or move routines to run after a reset.
  * Added an option to continue a chat after its limit resets, plus automatic recovery using an eligible backup engine.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of usage-limit refusals so unfinished turns can be resumed and recovery respects reset timing.

items.title: Import a shared Grok Bot, plus a Settings → Import page
items.body:
## What this does

Brings a shared Grok Bot (`https://x.ai/bot/<id>`) into Maus as an ordinary template import. One shared component (`GrokImportFlow`) does it in three places:

- **Templates → Import → From Grok Bot**
- **Settings → Import**: a new page, described below
- the welcome tour's import step, as an optional row

### The flow

1. **Paste the link.** The link can go in the new Grok box, in the GitHub box, or come from `openmausbot://install?url=https://x.ai/bot/<id>`. The server reads the public page and the box shows a card: name, creator, description.
2. **Copy export prompt.** One line under it says "Paste this into your Grok Bot, then paste its reply here". The person's own Grok Bot replies with one JSON block (`"format": "openmaus.grok/1"`).
3. **Paste the reply.** The usual template preview opens, and **Add** goes through the existing `/api/teams/import?mode=add`.
4. **Start from description** is for someone without Grok Bot. It makes a bot from the public name and description alone, credited "Based on x.ai/bot/<id>".
5. **Sign in with Cursor to import everything** (optional, one click). The person signs in to their own Cursor account in their browser. After that, the card loads the full bot and the preview opens straight away. A small "Signed in to Cursor · Sign out" line sits on the card. If anything fails, the card and steps 2–4 stay, with one short line saying why.
6. **After Add**, if the bot has apps to connect or something was left out, the panel offers **Have your Chief of Staff finish the setup**. Without a Chief, it offers the imported bot instead. That opens the chat with a message prepared but not sent. The message names the bot and link, the apps to connect (with their Composio names), Grok tools with no match, and the left-out routines with their original text.

The copy-paste path always works, signed in or not.

### Settings → Import (new page, next to Backups)

- **From your AI apps:** Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop and Gemini. This is the welcome tour's importer, not a second one: the same `ImportRow`s, the same `setupImportApi` client and the same `/api/setup-import` route (local desktop only). Tools arrive switched off, and logins and history are never read.
- **From Grok Bot:** the shared flow, done inline here: card, Cursor sign-in or export prompt, reply, preview, Add, then the Chief finishes the setup.
- **Where it shows:**
  - Desktop app only.
  - In Advanced mode it sits after Backups.
  - In Simple mode it is on the Account page; Simple mode stays at five pages.

### Welcome tour

The existing import step (`ImportBeat`) gets one more row: **Grok Bot**, "Have a Grok Bot? Paste its link".

- It opens the same Grok flow inline.
- **Not now** closes it again, and Skip still works.
- There is no new step, and skills plus tools work exactly as before.

### The Grok Bot mark

- **Source:** the symbol in the "Grok Bot" wordmark (`<svg aria-label="Grok Bot" viewBox="0 0 371 70">`, the last `fill-rule="evenodd"` path) in the header of the public share page https://x.ai/bot/d8OshqLZvtcKDcNluPuyo. It was fetched once without a login into an empty folder, and it is byte-identical to the research copy.
- **Why this mark:** the repo already had `GrokMark` (xAI's Grok engine logo). Grok Bot uses a different mark: a filled circle with two eyes. The `grok-bot-mark` shapes on the share page are each bot's own avatar, not the brand.
- **What was kept:** only the path data, checked to be path commands and numbers. It lives in `src/components/GrokBotMark.tsx`, next to `CursorMark` and re-exported from `ProviderIcons`, filled with `var(--color-ink)` so it themes in dark mode.
- **Where it shows:** the box heading, the loaded card, the "Sign in with Cursor to import everything" button, the Settings section and the welcome row.

### What's imported (`shared/grok-import.ts` → `openmaus.package` v2, validated by `shared/package-format.ts`)

| Grok | Maus |
|---|---|
| name, description | `agents[0]`, `package.name`, `tagline`, `summary`, `team.name` |
| instructions | `agents[0].soul`, cut at 24,000 bytes, with a Left out note |
| skills | `SKILL.md` entries with generated frontmatter (a body's own frontmatter is replaced). At most 30. They arrive **off** |
| routines with a cron, or a plain time ("weekdays at 9am") | `routines[]`, `runOn: maus`, **paused**. A missing or unknown zone falls back to the computer's |
| event routines, or schedules that can't be read | listed under **Left out** with their original text |
| plugins | `requirements.apps`, with Composio slugs when known (gmail, slack, github, googlecalendar…) and labels otherwise |
| memories | `seed` `MEMORY.md`, only when present (the prompt says "Include memories: no" by default) |
| colour | nearest bot colour |
| model, computer, logins, MCP | never |

Package fields filled in by Maus:

- `id`: name slug plus a short hash
- `release`: 1.0.0
- `category`: Imported
- `license`: See source
- `setupMinutes`: 5
- `author`: the creator, linking to the x.ai URL

Key-shaped text is redacted (and listed). The parser is forgiving:

- It tolerates a code fence and chat around the JSON.
- It also reads pi-grokbot-import's `grokbot-bundle/v1`, pasted or dropped as a `.json` file.

### Why there's no one-click import without signing in

The public page holds only `{id, ownerType, sharerName, botName, description, color, shape}`: its embedded data and og tags carry nothing else. The instructions, skills and routines come either from the person's own Grok Bot (the export prompt) or from Cursor's `GetGrokBotTemplateImportDetails`, which needs a signed-in Cursor session.

### Cursor sign-in (`server/cursor-session.ts`)

- **Sign-in.** Cursor's CLI-style PKCE browser flow:
  - `cursor.com/loginDeepControl?challenge&uuid&mode=login&redirectTarget=cli` opens in the person's own browser.
  - `GET api2.cursor.sh/auth/poll` runs once per status check while waiting, and stops after 10 minutes.
- **Fetching the template.**
  - `POST api2.cursor.sh/aiserver.v1.GrokBotService/GetGrokBotTemplateImportDetails` with `{shareId}` and `Authorization: Bearer`.
  - The signed `blobGetUrl` is then downloaded **without** the token. It must be public https, and redirects are refused.
- **Mapping.** The recipe is mapped into the same `openmaus.grok/1` shape the paste produces, so `grokExportToPackage` and the preview do the rest.
- **Where the token lives.**
  - It is stored in `<data dir>/cursor-session.json` with mode 0600, and never in a response or a log. A held-value scrubber masks it in anything the app redacts.
  - It is sent only to `https://api2.cursor.sh`: the origin is pinned and api2 redirects are refused.
  - On a 401, or when the JWT expires, it is deleted. **Sign out** deletes it too.
- **Credit.** Request and response shapes come from [pi-grokbot-import](https://github.com/Shixuuu/pi-grokbot-import) by Shixuuu (MIT per its package.json; the repo has no LICENSE file). They are reimplemented here, and the module header credits it.
- **Unverified.** `api2.cursor.sh` is unlisted, and the recipe shape here is taken from pi-grokbot-import's source, not from a live call. The research also noted that the third-party terms reportedly bar re-exporting someone else's bot without the creator's OK. The Cursor path is optional, and the copy-paste path never depends on it.

### Routes (all admin scope by the default-deny rule, like the GitHub import)

- `POST /api/team-library/grok` `{url}`:
  - Fetches only `https://x.ai/bot/<id>`, from either the x.ai link or the `grokbot://app/v1/bot-template?id=` link.
  - Redirects are followed by hand, only while they stay on `x.ai`/`www.x.ai` over https, at most 3.
  - 20 s timeout and a 2 MB streamed cap.
  - It reads the embedded record first, then the og tags.
  - When signed in to Cursor, the answer also carries `export` or `exportNote`.
- `GET /api/team-library/cursor`, `POST /api/team-library/cursor/sign-in`, `POST /api/team-library/cursor/sign-out`.

Nothing registers `grokbot://`, and nothing reads other apps' files or stored logins. Overlap check: #614 (Aug, a fork) imports public instructions from an undocumented protobuf endpoint; this PR doesn't build on it.

### Files

- **This round:**
  - New:
    - `src/components/GrokImportFlow.tsx` (shared flow)
    - `src/components/ImportSettings.tsx`
    - `src/components/GrokBotMark.tsx`
    - `src/components/TeamImportDetails.tsx`, moved out of `TeamLibraryPanel` and still re-exported there
    - `src/lib/template-add.ts`: the Add call, now shared by Templates and the flow
  - Changed:
    - `src/components/SettingsModal.tsx`: stays at its 1061-line pin, because two `case` lines were folded
    - `src/state/store.tsx`: the section union, at its pin
    - `onboarding/beats/ImportBeat.tsx`
    - `src/components/TeamLibraryPanel.tsx`: now 971 lines, off the ratchet list
    - `en.json`, `docs/team-sharing.md`
- **Earlier rounds:**

- New:
  - `shared/grok-import.ts`
  - `server/cursor-session.ts`
  - `src/components/GrokImportBox.tsx`
  - `src/components/GrokFinishSetup.tsx`
  - tests for each
  - `server/routes/team-library-grok.test.ts`
  - `server/fixtures/grok-share-page*.html`: trimmed copies of two real share pages
- Changed:
  - `server/team-library.ts`: `fetchGrokTemplateCard`
  - `server/routes/teams.ts`
  - `src/lib/team-import.ts`
  - `src/components/TeamLibraryPanel.tsx`: 1097 → 1091 lines, ratchet pin lowered
  - `electron/package-link.mjs` (+ node test)
  - `src/locales/en.json`
  - `docs/team-sharing.md` ("From Grok Bot")

## Tests

No network: every fetch is stubbed, and the x.ai pages are trimmed fixtures.

- **Share links:** x.ai with or without www, a trailing slash or a query, `grokbot://`. Other hosts, http, credentials, ports, extra paths, `marketplace` and short ids are refused.
- **Parsers:** `openmaus.grok/1` (fenced, bare, BOM, a skill body with its own fence), `grokbot-bundle/v1`, Cursor recipes, and garbage input with a clear sentence.
- **Mapping:**
  - the package is valid
  - the instructions cut at 24 KB with a note
  - the 30-skill and 50-routine caps
  - skill frontmatter
  - cron, daily and zone fallback; event and unreadable routines Left out with their original text
  - Composio slugs, memories seed, key redaction
  - no model
  - author and id
- **Card fetcher:**
  - the embedded record, and the og fallback
  - no fetch for a foreign link
  - redirects on and off host
  - 2 MB cap, both announced and streamed
  - 404, timeout
- **Route:** admin scope, card passthrough, 400/404.
- **Cursor:**
  - PKCE parameters (the challenge is sha256 of the verifier, and the verifier never goes to the login page)
  - poll until approved, the 10-minute timeout, refusal
  - the 0600 file
  - the token never in a status, route response or console output, and masked by the redactor
  - host pin: the bearer goes only to `api2.cursor.sh`, and the blob download carries no token; http, IP and localhost blob URLs are refused
  - fallback on 401 (the session is deleted), a bad shape, non-JSON, blob 403, details 500 and no network
  - sign-out removes the stored session
  - an expired JWT is forgotten without a call
- **UI** (static render):
  - the card with creator, the export-prompt line, the reply box, Start from description
  - the Cursor sign-in, waiting and signed-in lines
  - Left out titled in the preview
  - the finish-setup step, and the prepared message (put ahead of any draft, never sent; the Chief, or the imported bot)
- **Mutation-checked:** each of these was broken on purpose, and a test failed every time:
  - the share-link host check, the redirect host check, manual redirects, the stream cap
  - routines paused, event routines left out, soul shortening
  - the agent holding its skills, Composio slugs, secret redaction, the author link, the preview recognising a Grok export

- **This round:**
  - Settings → Import draws both sections in order, and From your AI apps covers its states: looking, nothing new, not this computer, and the result.
  - The Settings rail and Simple-mode placement tests are updated.
  - The welcome row opens the flow inline, closes with Not now, can be skipped while open, and adds no checkbox or step.
  - Templates, Settings and the welcome step all use `GrokImportFlow`, and none uses the box directly. The flow starts framed or bare.
  - The mark shows in its three box places.
  - The logo is a sanitised static asset: only `svg` + `path`, no script, `on*=`, href, xlink, `url()`, `data:`, style or `foreignObject`. Its path data is commands and numbers only.

Ran (head 88de1c036):

- `pnpm typecheck` ✓
- `pnpm lint` ✓
- `pnpm i18n:check` ✓; main had no ja failure
- file-size and index-route ratchets ✓
- `electron/package-link.node-test.mjs` ✓
- touched and related vitest files: 41 files, 371 tests ✓

The full suite was not run, as asked; CI runs it.

Not run: the Electron app itself (never launched), and no live x.ai or Cursor calls.

* **New Features**
  * Import Grok Bot templates from share or marketplace links during onboarding or from Settings and Templates, or create a starter bot from its public description.
  * Preview imported content and see what could not be carried over. Copy a prompt to request export details, paste a JSON response, or optionally sign in to Cursor to load the full template.
  * After import, optionally open a prepared, unsent setup message in a Chief of Staff or the imported bot’s chat.
  * Import detected skills and tools from AI apps in Settings when running locally.
* **Documentation**
  * Added guidance for importing Grok Bot templates and using the available import options.
